title: Rabbah son of Rav Huna Zuta of Nehardea
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was the judge there, as in Ketubot 69a, where Rav Nechemyah son of Rav Yosef sent to him: “When that woman comes before you, collect a tenth of the property for her.” Hyman identifies Rav Nechemyah as Rava’s student and infers that Rabbah son of Rav Huna Zuta was head in Nehardea in Rav Papa’s time.

Likewise in Beitzah 29b: “Rava [Hyman proposes Rabbah, as in the Soncino printing and the She’iltot, Emor] son of Rav Huna Zuti expounded at the gate of Nehardea. Rav Nachman said: Go out and tell Abba (my colleague — Rashi): We owe you no thanks for this,” etc. (Hyman considers “Rav Nachman” a scribal error and proposes, according to Dikdukei Soferim, Rav Chama; he endorses this reading, for Rav Chama too was head in Nehardea after Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 2.)

notes.text: Saved Vilna Rashi Beitzah29b explains שקילא טיבותיך as owing no thanks for the proposed favor, not the literal favor being taken. Hyman’s competing Rav Nachman/Rav Chama and Rava/Rabbah readings remain attributed; the Soncino report is not newly pixel-verified.

The consulted Vilna Rashi Beitzah 29b explains Abba as my colleague and the idiom as owing no thanks. Hyman’s judge/head chronology and Rav Nachman/Rav Chama, Rava/Rabbah, Soncino, She’iltot, Dikdukei Soferim and Iggeret claims remain separately attributed; exact editions were not inspected here.
